subject: Capacity incident: Dedicated GPU cluster saturation — billing adjustment & postmortem plan
messages:
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@luminahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Capacity incident: Dedicated GPU cluster saturation — immediate update

Jordan — quick update from the platform side. We observed sustained saturation in one of the Dedicated GPU pools that services a subset of LuminaHealth reserved capacity between 08:40 and 09:05 ET this morning. Symptoms: elevated queue times and token-level latency spikes for a subset of inference routes (primarily long-context document summarization) causing degraded throughput for requests pinned to that pool.

What happened (short):
- Autoscaler hit a limit on reserved nodes while warmup was in progress — new nodes did not become available quickly enough for the burst pattern.
- Continuous batching backpressure was amplified by a few long-running requests holding KV shards, which reduced effective slot utilization.

Immediate mitigations we executed:
- Shifted affected routes to a cold-fallback pool (compatible model variant) at 08:52 ET to restore steady throughput.
- Throttled largest client prefixes for 10 minutes to reduce KV lock hold time (08:55–09:05 ET).
- Manually increased reserved node headroom for LuminaHealth to +15% for the next 24h while we validate autoscale policy changes.

Impact: short window (~25 minutes) of elevated latency for a subset of requests. No data exposure, no failed writes.

Attachments: incident_dashboard.png (short dashboard snapshot), resource-logs-20260712.zip (engine traces + node metrics).

Next steps: Marcus will follow with technical root-cause and short-term fixes. I will coordinate billing/credit discussion with you and share our postmortem draft tomorrow. We have a 30-minute call open at 11:30 ET if you can join.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLA expectations and are prioritizing both remediation and compensation.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity incident: Dedicated GPU cluster saturation — immediate update

Thanks — additional technical detail for the thread and Lumina team.

Root cause (prelim):
- The autoscaler had an aggressive cooldown configured for that Dedicated pool after recent rapid scaling events; combined with a subtle regression in our warmup scheduler (introduced in 2026-06-28 release) the new nodes were delayed (~90s extra) in entering the ready pool.
- Two customer sessions with unusually long contexts (130k tokens) held KV cache and prevented effective batching. Those sessions created head-of-line blocking for ~3 worker shards.

Why this mattered: the reserved-node headroom had been sized to normal operating variance. The combination of delayed warmup + head-of-line locking pushed the pool to saturation faster than our predicted tail distributions.

Actions taken (short-term):
- Disabled the warmup regression on the affected fleet (rolled out at 09:10 ET).
- Adjusted autoscaler cooldown for the pool from 300s -> 60s as an emergency policy change to allow quicker node add.
- Implemented per-session soft-limits for KV retention for long contexts (temporary throttle) to prevent future shard hogging.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Rework warmup scheduler to prefetch kernel states asynchronously (Q3 milestone).
- Add model-aware headroom recommendations to Redwood Optimize so reserved pools self-tune headroom based on context-length distribution.

I'll drop the trace slices and patch release notes into the Drive link shortly.

— Marcus
SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@luminahealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity incident: Dedicated GPU cluster saturation — immediate update

Vanessa / Marcus — thanks for the quick notice and the mitigation. A couple of questions from our ops and procurement teams:

1) We saw customer-impact during the 08:40–09:05 window. Given this is a Reserved Dedicated pool under an SLA, what is Redwood's approach to crediting for this downtime? We will need a credit proposal to evaluate with our finance team.

2) What changes will you commit to in the near term to reduce recurrence risk? The technical summary helps but we need concrete timelines we can share with our stakeholders.

3) Can you confirm the temporary headroom increase (+15%) is already in effect and will it remain until your postmortem is completed?

We can join the 11:30 ET call — Jordan + infra lead will be on.

— Jordan Price
Head of Platform | LuminaHealth
jordan.price@luminahealth.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@luminahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity incident: Dedicated GPU cluster saturation — immediate update

Jordan — thanks. Short answers:

1) Credits: We will propose a goodwill credit covering the impacted window and the incremental compute cost from the emergency headroom. Preliminary proposal: a one-time credit equal to 3x the estimated token-cost during the 25-minute impact window (we calculate both the latency penalty and the fallback variant delta). We will follow up with a formal credit note by EOD. If that proposal doesn't fit your procurement process, we can escalate for an exception.

2) Near-term commitments (timelines):
- Immediate: keep +15% headroom for 24h (in place now).
- 72h: revert emergency autoscale cooldown and deploy a targeted patch to avoid the warmup regression on all affected pools (Marcus timing: rolling patch within 36h, full fleet by 72h).
- 30 days: publish a customer-facing postmortem and an action plan including the warmup scheduler fix and Optimize recommendations.

3) Headroom: confirmed — +15% applied now and we will keep it for the next 24h; if you prefer an extended window while we complete the patching, we can extend to 72h.

Call: joining 11:30 ET is great — I'll share a short slide with the timeline and credit preview during the call.

— Vanessa

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Postmortem draft & next steps — LuminaHealth Dedicated pool incident (07/12)

Jordan — thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Attached is our postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-20260713.pdf) with full timeline, root cause analysis, impact metrics, and proposed remediation schedule. High-level items:

- Timeline: incident start 08:40 ET, fallback shift 08:52 ET, emergency policies applied 08:55–09:10 ET, resolved 09:05 ET for customer-visible latency; warmup regression disabled fleet-wide by 11:00 ET.
- Root cause: combined autoscale cooldown + warmup regression + head-of-line KV retention from long-context sessions.
- Customer impact: increased median latency on affected routes from 280ms -> 1.8s for the 25-minute window; no errors or dropped requests logged.
- Short-term remediation: autoscaler cooldown policy adjustment, warmup regression rollback, temporary per-session KV soft-limits, +15% headroom for 72h (extended at customer request).
- Long-term remediation: asynchronous kernel prefetching (Q3), Optimize integration for model-aware headroom (Q3/Q4), and enhanced observability for session-level KV retention (Q3).

Requested actions for LuminaHealth:
- Please review the draft and flag any inaccuracies by EOD tomorrow.
- Confirm whether you would like the +15% headroom extended to 72h (we currently have it set to expire 07/13 09:15 ET).
- Approve the proposed credit calculation so finance can issue a formal credit note.

We have scheduled a follow-up on Thurs 07/15 14:00 ET to review the final postmortem and remediation schedule. Link: https://meet.redwood.ai/8921-review.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20260713.pdf.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
